title: tau upgrade --json output
description: Schema for the single JSON object `tau upgrade [--json]` prints on stdout. The report is emitted for every outcome — success, skip, and failure — and the process exit code maps from status: up_to_date/upgraded/declined/dry_run -> 0, skipped/failed -> 1 (exit 111 on Windows, where the command is unimplemented). New keys may be added (additive); existing keys keep their names and types.

version.description: Version of the running binary before the upgrade, e.g. "0.4.0".

checked.description: Whether the release lookup actually ran — false when the check is disabled (TAU_NO_UPDATE_CHECK) or curl is unavailable.

latest.description: Latest released version string when the lookup found one.

tag.description: Release tag for the latest version (e.g. "v0.5.0") when the lookup found one.

update_available.description: true when the latest release is newer than the running binary. Emitted only when checked is true.

status.description: Outcome of the run. up_to_date: already on the latest release; upgraded: the installer ran and exited 0; declined: the user answered no at the TTY prompt; skipped: the check was disabled or a non-interactive run lacked --yes; failed: the lookup, download, or install errored; dry_run: --dry-run reported the plan without touching anything.

detail.description: Human-readable outcome detail — what happened or why nothing did; informational, may be reworded.

release_url.description: Release page URL for the newer version; present only when update_available is true.

install_dir.description: Resolved install destination (--dir > TAU_INSTALL_DIR > the running binary's directory); absent when the installer default applied.

changelog.description: Release-notes sections lifted from the target tag's CHANGELOG.md covering versions in (installed, latest]. Present only when the best-effort fetch produced at least one matching section.

version.description: Version of the changelog section, e.g. "0.5.0".

notes.description: Section body verbatim — the release notes for that version.

examples.name: tau
examples.detail: would install tau 0.5.0 via https://example/install.sh into ~/.local/bin
